commitments.statement: Greater TMT diversity leads to superior firm performance.
commitments.origin_note: Prevailing view, but direct effects often null (Bell et al. 2011; Fox et al. 2022).

updates.description: Doubt: Repeated null direct effects plus backlash undercut the broad claim.
Execution: Firm+year FE estimate of diversity->ROA is -0.05755 (95% CI [-0.13267, 0.01757], p=0.1332); data favor the null over the belief-predicted +0.05 effect (LR=0.06).

commitments.statement: Diversity's effect is mediated by the firm's competitive actions (variety/complexity/calibration).
commitments.origin_note: Core mechanism in Fox et al. 2022 and the Ferrier lineage.

commitments.statement: There is little/no DIRECT diversity->performance effect; it operates indirectly.
commitments.origin_note: Direct effects n.s. in Fox et al. 2022 and Ferrier 2001.

updates.description: Execution: Same FE estimate: tight CI around zero is evidence FOR a null direct effect.

commitments.statement: Diversity's benefit is contingent and non-monotonic (requisite variety; moderation), not 'more is better'.
commitments.origin_note: Ferrier & Lyon 2004 moderation; Fox 2022 requisite variety; Ferrier 2001 U-shapes.

commitments.statement: Experiential/task-relevant variety matters more than demographic diversity for performance.
commitments.origin_note: Fox 2022 gender diversity n.s.; Crossland career variety.

commitments.statement: Diverse TMTs make higher-quality decisions via broader information processing and constructive conflict.
commitments.origin_note: Upper-echelons premise; support indirect/mixed.

updates.description: Doubt: Decision-quality premise is questioned by the merit critique.

commitments.statement: TMT diversity is not achieved at the expense of average member competence (diversity vs. merit not in tension).
commitments.origin_note: Implicit, rarely tested; directly challenged by the anomaly.

updates.description: Doubt: Competence-dilution mechanism directly contradicts the implicit no-tradeoff assumption.

commitments.statement: Diversity's performance benefit requires experiential variety + action calibration; demographic diversity alone is null/negative.
commitments.origin_note: Warranted by the FE fit + exploration in this cycle.

commitments.statement: Demographic diversity erodes via a promotion-turnover asymmetry (build-leak).
commitments.origin_note: Warranted by the build-vs-leak finding.

doubts.description: [perceived_gaps] Upper-echelons theory lacks a diversity-competence tradeoff: it credits diversity with cognitive variety but is silent on whether diversity-driven selection lowers average ability.

[unsolved_puzzles] The current best model cannot explain why direct diversity->performance effects are repeatedly null while diversity is still prescribed - suggesting an unmodeled offsetting negative (competence/coordination) path.
[unexpected_behavior] Widespread DEI rollback and the meritocracy critique: boards/executives increasingly act as if diversity is performance-costly, contrary to prevailing belief.
[anomalous_observations] Diversity-performance correlations appear to weaken or reverse in recent samples and in quasi-experimental (mandate/ban) settings.

bam.description: Moderated-mediation prototype: TMT experiential variety -> calibration/quality of competitive actions -> performance, with an offsetting competence-dilution path that can cancel the variety path.

components.statement: Upper-echelons: TMT cognition shapes strategic action
Requisite variety: action variety must match environmental variety
Direct diversity->performance effects are repeatedly null
Action complexity->performance is U-shaped, not monotonic
Competence-dilution: diversity-via-selection can lower average ability

hypotheses: Net variety-vs-competence: diversity helps when it adds experiential variety without lowering average competence, and hurts when it does.
Calibration: diversity helps only when it calibrates competitive-action variety to environmental variety; DEI-driven diversity uncorrelated with requisite variety yields no benefit.
Two opposing mediated paths (variety->better actions +; competence-dilution->worse execution -) cancel, explaining null direct effects.
Type-of-diversity: experiential/task-relevant diversity is positive; demographic-only diversity decoupled from experience is null/negative.
Context-contingent: in high-backlash/low-trust settings, diversity raises coordination and legitimacy costs that suppress action execution.

troves.description: TMT composition + executive bios (experiential variety & competence proxies)
Firm performance (ROA, market-share change) + DEI policy events

techniques.description: NLP on bios/disclosures for competence + experiential variety
Causal forest & quasi-experimental estimators on DEI mandate/ban variation

explorations.summary: Demographic diversity -> ROA is ~null across all scopes (within-firm ~0); minorities (esp. Black) leak via turnover faster than they are built via promotion.

consistent.note: direct effect near zero across all three scopes

credible.note: firmwide 95% CI [-0.13267, 0.01757] brackets 0 and excludes the belief-predicted 0.05

validation.summary: within-firm FE + cross-scope consistency as robustness

metrics.model: ROA ~ blau_race + prop_f + log(assets) + leverage + firm FE + year FE (cluster SE by firm)

bam.description: TMT diversity enhances firm performance chiefly INDIRECTLY, by shaping the variety, complexity, and calibration of the firm's competitive actions; benefits are contingent (requisite fit to environmental variety), not a direct or monotonic effect of diversity, and stem more from experiential than demographic diversity.

spec.literature_summary: Fox/Simsek/Heavey 2022 (experiential variety -> calibrated repertoire -> ROA; direct effect null); Ferrier 2001 (heterogeneity -> some attack dims; no direct effect; U-shaped complexity); Ferrier & Lyon 2004 (heterogeneity moderates simplicity->performance); Crossland 2014 (CEO career variety -> novelty, not TMT heterogeneity; volatility not level).
spec.researcher_summary: Diversity of background/experience helps TMTs navigate complex decisions, improving performance.
